doc: Phasor arithmetic. The only area that touches no file, so nothing here can be skipped for want of data -- which makes it the cheapest possible check that a binding is wired up at all. The IRF-referenced g and s are a rotation and scaling of the raw phasor, so passing an identity IRF (g=1, s=0) must return the experimental values unchanged.

cases.doc: With g_irf = 1 and s_irf = 0 the IRF correction is the identity, so g and s come back as they went in. A binding that swapped the argument order would fail this and nothing else.
A non-identity IRF, where g and s genuinely mix. Asymmetric inputs throughout, so a transposed or reordered argument list cannot pass by coincidence.
A single-exponential decay in 32 bins, reduced to one (g, s) pair. This is the vector-in, vector-out path rather than the scalar one.
An empty histogram cannot yield a phasor. What comes back is the documented not-a-value pair rather than an exception, so a caller scanning an image does not have to guard every pixel.
